issues.description: Method return-type mismatch for Stock.take(String): The problem statement UML declares Stock.take(String): int (uses -1 as a failure sentinel). The solution implementation (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java) implements public int take(String) and returns -1 on failure or the remaining quantity on success. However, the template implementation (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java) declares public boolean take(String), returning true/false. This inconsistency will cause compilation errors or incorrect behavior when students implement SealSaloon logic because SealSaloon (solution) expects take(...) to return an int and checks for -1 (e.g., solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/SealSaloon.java calls stock.take(x) == -1).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template Stock.take signature and behavior match the UML and the solution: change the template method to 'public int take(String ingredient)'. Implement it to return -1 if the ingredient does not exist or if quantity < 1, otherwise decrement the stored quantity and return the remaining quantity. Update any template comments/tests to reflect the int return contract so students can implement SealSaloon.checkOrderReady using the -1 sentinel as shown in the specification and solution.
